content:
We release TheoremGraph, a sequel to TheoremSearch!

We collected the theorem-level dependency graph of arXiv, of mathlib, and of 25 other big Lean projects, and found declarations with the same mathematical content between the formal and informal parts of the graph. I really recommend watching the video below, especially if you like 3blue1brown!
This was done by the UW Math AI Lab.

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25363
Webpage: https://theoremsearch.com/theorem-graph
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H2z3VRRd4aQ

Nice video. The clear explanation and animations made this super accessible. My feeling is that we are in desperate need of tools like TheoremSearch, because agents will need to efficiently traverse across text-based informal reasoning space simultaneously with the formal Lean chessboard. It will be interesting to see how this area develops in competition with similar semantic search engines like LeanSearch or LeanExplore. I do have two questions:

1) What is the intended use case for the API? The entry point POST /search hosted on https://www.theoremsearch.com/search and provided in the MCP only returns informal arXiv results, not lean declaration, so I'm not sure how useful this is as an autoformalization tool. I was able to get some Lean identifiers using GET /graph/embedding + GET /graph/statement/{id} but there's no way to filter to only Mathlib declarations so the results are always polluted with informal statements. Finally, as far as I can tell there is no way to query the 48k exact/inexact GPT-judged matches between the formal<-->informal statements, which imo is the main novel result of the paper.

2) What is the motivation for not using a reranker? The paper's abstract advertises retrieval "without an LM reranker"--however the limitations section explicitly states this as something that could improve results:

Giving judges more context, such as the source paper, is a natural way to improve cross-corpus linking, alongside evaluating alternative slogan generators, embedding models, rerankers, and a broader judge panel. (pg. 10, emph added)

The data from LeanSearch v2 paper indicates a benchmark bump from reranking. Given that TheoremSearch is already using Qwen3-Embedding-8B to embed the query, is it really that much more costly to include Qwen3-Reranker-8B instead of cosine similarity? It feel like this choice needs justification.
